record.original_question: Does there exist a complete lattice with enough co-primes, equivalently a complete lattice isomorphic to the lattice of all closed subsets of some topological space, whose Scott topology is non-sober?

evidence.quote: Question 3.5. Is there a complete lattice with enough co-primes (i.e., isomorphic to the lattice of all closed subsets of a topological space) that has a non-sober Scott topology?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let L be a complete lattice. An element p ∈ L is called co-prime (or meet-irreducible in the dual sense) if p ≠ ⊤ and whenever p ≥ a ∧ b for a, b ∈ L, one has p ≥ a or p ≥ b (equivalently, taking the dual formulation: x is co-prime if x ≤ a ∨ b implies x ≤ a or x ≤ b). Say that L has enough co-primes if every element of L is the infimum (meet) of co-primes lying above it. It is known that a complete lattice has enough co-primes if and only if it is isomorphic to the lattice C(X) of all closed subsets of some topological space X, ordered by inclusion.

The Scott topology σ(L) on L has as open sets those U ⊆ L which are upper sets (x ∈ U and x ≤ y imply y ∈ U) and inaccessible by directed suprema (whenever D ⊆ L is a directed set with sup D ∈ U, then D ∩ U ≠ ∅). A topological space (Y, τ) is sober if every nonempty irreducible closed set (a closed set that is not the union of two proper closed subsets) is the closure of a unique point.

Question: Does there exist a complete lattice L with enough co-primes — equivalently, a complete lattice isomorphic to the lattice of all closed subsets of some topological space — such that the Scott topology σ(L) on L is not sober?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches indicate this is a known open problem in non-Hausdorff topology / domain theory, often attributed to Xu and Zhao. While related counterexamples to Scott sobriety exist (Isbell's complete lattice; countable distributive lattices by Miao–Xi–Li–Zhao; complete Heyting algebras by Xu–Xi–Zhao), the specific question of whether a lattice of closed sets of some topological space (i.e., a complete lattice with enough co-primes) can have a non-sober Scott topology does not appear to have been resolved in the literature accessible via search.

status_evidence.title: Not every countable complete lattice is sober
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of countable Scott non-sober distributive complete lattices, but does not address the lattice-of-closed-sets restriction.
status_evidence.claim: Related counterexamples are known but not for lattices with enough co-primes.

status_evidence.title: The Scott space of lattice of closed subsets with supremum operator
status_evidence.snippet: Studies σ(C(X)) and related Scott topology properties; lists explicit open problems.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work studies C(X) but does not settle whether σ(C(X)) can fail to be sober.

status_evidence.title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems regarding sobriety of Scott topologies on various lattices.
status_evidence.claim: The question is recorded as open in the survey.
